name: The Iron Bridge
hint: Boats need the middle of the gorge: no piers. Spring an arch from the low anchors on the banks and stand the road on it.

history.name: The Iron Bridge
history.engineer: Thomas Farnolls Pritchard (design), Abraham Darby III (ironmaster)
facts: Its nearly 1,700 cast parts - about 378 tons of iron - were joined with carpentry joints such as mortise-and-tenon and dovetails, because nobody had built in iron before.
A single span kept the busy river clear for boat traffic.
It closed to vehicles in 1934 and is part of the Ironbridge Gorge UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986).
history.why: The first major bridge in the world made of cast iron - the moment bridges started to be built from metal.
history.note: Cast iron is not in the game: build the arch from wood and steel.
